body:
GCG, which specializes in wire and cable distribution for demanding applications, has agreed to be purchased by Rexel from Audax Private Equity, the company said in a press release. Completion of the deal is anticipated before the calendar year ends.

The business runs two complementary units, Custom Engineered Solutions and Connectivity & Power Solutions, supplying engineer-driven wire, cable and connectivity offerings to clients in data centers, power infrastructure, defense, building systems, water, telecom and industrial sectors. From 2019 onward, GCG expanded to surpass $1.1 billion in revenue, growing both organically and through acquisitions such as United Wire & Cable, CableMaster, RWL, Paige and Allied Wire & Cable.

Chief executive officer Glenn Pennycook called the transaction an important milestone and attributed it to the company's business, culture and workforce. He said Audax's backing allowed GCG to develop a distinctive operation with technical strengths, ties to customers and suppliers, and a history of expansion. Pennycook also stated that Rexel's strategic priorities and dedication to customers and suppliers position it as the appropriate partner to maintain that trajectory and generate fresh prospects for employees, clients and supplier partners.

The deal is anticipated to broaden Rexel's footprint in fast-growing, mission-critical sectors like data center and power infrastructure, while integrating GCG's engineering-focused distribution approach and proprietary product range into Rexel's larger platform.

Audax Private Equity originally obtained GCG via a carveout of Genuine Parts Company's Electrical Specialties Group. Audax assisted in setting up and collaborating with GCG's leadership to develop the platform through organic growth efforts and a systematic acquisition approach, finishing several add-on deals.

Solomon Partners and J.P. Morgan acted as financial advisors to GCG and Audax for the sale, with Kirkland & Ellis and Fredrikson & Byron supplying legal counsel. Guggenheim Securities and Rothschild & Company were financial advisors to Rexel, and Sidley Austin LLP provided legal advice.

GCG is based in Chicago, Illinois, and runs its regional brands across North America and Europe via 16 sites with over 950 staff. The company is projected to exceed $1.1 billion in revenue during 2026.

Rexel is a global specialist in multichannel professional distribution of energy-related products and services, serving residential, non-residential and industrial markets. The group assists customers with a customized and expandable array of energy management products and services for construction, renovation, production and maintenance. Rexel has 1,876 branches across 17 countries with 26,306 employees, and its 2025 sales totaled €19.4 billion.

Audax Private Equity is based in Boston with locations in San Francisco, New York, London and Hong Kong. The firm invests throughout the North American middle market and aims to speed up value creation via its Buy & Build strategy and the Audax Value Agenda. As of July 2026, Audax Private Equity managed roughly $20.1 billion in assets and, since starting in 1999, has invested in over 180 platforms and more than 1,500 add-on acquisitions.
